title: State School Scores
scope: This ledger ranks states on NCES Digest public K-12 enrollment for Fall 2024, and also reports the 2021-22 adjusted cohort graduation rate, the 2020-21 out-of-school suspension and expulsion shares (including the published race and ethnicity columns), NAEP state reading and math average scale scores for grades 4 and 8 from the first state assessment through 2024 (including 2019-to-2024 and 2022-to-2024 change), and NCES NPEFS FY 2024 current expenditures per pupil.
exclusions: Does not cover Massachusetts-only DESE files (those sit on Massachusetts Schools) or higher education. In-school suspension is not a column on Digest table 233.40.
heritage: Formerly Reading/Math Achievement, K-12 Enrollment, K-12 School Finance, High School Completion, and Discipline & Security
vintage_note: Rebuilt Aug 15, 2026 from NCES Digest 2025 table 203.20. U.S. Fall 2024 enrollment equals 49,387,403. Later views compiled Aug 15, 2026 are stored under derived.secondary. Tableau companions compiled Aug 16, 2026 are stored under derived.secondary.

q: NAEP scores, enrollment, school finance, graduation, and discipline, including suspension by race, across the fifty states.
lead: Public elementary and secondary enrollment was 49,387,403 in the United States in Fall 2024 (SRC-607-02). Massachusetts enrolled 915,932, rank 17 of 51 (derived, SRC-607-02). The public high school 4-year graduation rate was 86.6% in 2021-22 (SRC-607-03). Massachusetts was 90.1%, rank 5 of 48 (derived, SRC-607-03). Out-of-school suspensions reached 1.32% of U.S. public-school students in 2020-21; Massachusetts was 0.59% (SRC-607-04). On the 2024 NAEP, grade-4 reading averaged 214.3 in the national public sample; Massachusetts scored 224.8, rank 1 of 51 (SRC-607-05). Grade-4 math was 237.3 nationally and 246.5 in Massachusetts (SRC-607-05). Grade-8 reading was 256.7 / 268.0; grade-8 math was 272.2 / 283.5 (SRC-607-05). From 2019 to 2024, national public grade-4 reading changed -5.2 points; 2 of 51 states rose and 49 fell (SRC-607-05). Louisiana had the largest grade-4 reading gain at +6.1 (SRC-607-05). Grade-8 math changed -8.8 nationally; 0 states rose (SRC-607-05). Expulsions reached 0.06% of U.S. public-school students in 2020-21; Massachusetts was 0.01% (SRC-607-07). NCES NPEFS current expenditures per pupil were $17,644 in the United States in FY 2024 (SRC-607-06). Massachusetts was $27,008, rank 5 of 51 (derived, SRC-607-06). Among Black students, the out-of-school suspension share was 2.32% nationally and 0.79% in Massachusetts (SRC-607-04).
